title: Frontend mid systemdesign client caching strategy
topic: Frontend mid systemdesign client caching strategy
question: Design a client-side caching strategy for an app where several screens display overlapping data fetched from the same API, e.g. a user's profile shown in a header, a sidebar, and a settings page.
idealAnswer:
Introduce a shared client-side cache keyed by resource identity (e.g. by user id) so multiple components requesting the same data reuse one cached entry instead of firing duplicate requests

Define a staleness policy per resource type, some data (like a user's display name) can be cached longer than something like a live notification count, this shouldn't be one-size-fits-all

Handle cache invalidation explicitly: when a mutation updates the user (e.g. editing settings), the cache entry must be updated or invalidated so all screens reflect the change, not just the screen that made the edit

Deduplicate in-flight requests, if two components request the same uncached resource simultaneously, they should share one network request rather than firing two

Decide a fallback/loading strategy: show stale-while-revalidate (old data immediately, refreshed in background) versus a loading spinner, this is a real UX tradeoff, not just an implementation detail

Mentions that this is largely a solved problem via libraries like React Query, SWR, or Apollo's cache, and a strong answer explains why to use one of these vs. hand-rolling it, or explicitly justifies hand-rolling for a specific reason
